newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Danish PM to propose EU treaty referendum.
newsitem.headline: Danish PM to propose EU treaty referendum.

text.p: Danish Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said he would propose to parliament that a referendum should be held on the outcome of the European Union reform talks which were concluded earlier on Wednesday.
"Yes, there will be a referendum. That will be my proposal to parliament," Rasmussen told reporters.
Rasmussen said the referendum would be held in 1998. Danish Economy Minister Marianne Jelved said on Monday she believed the public vote could be held in February or March.

Denmark, traditionally cool towards closer EU integration, threw the 15-nation bloc into chaos and confusion five years ago when its voters rejected the Maastricht treaty, which had beens agreed in the Dutch town of the same name in 1991.
The Danes accepted the treaty in a new vote the following year, but only after their government negotiated opt-outs from some of its key aims, including economic and monetary union (EMU).
The revised treaty agreed in Amsterdam is seen as much less far-reaching than the Maastricht treaty, which laid down the path towards EMU.
